about.title: Burbank Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Burbank looks different from one block to the next: production crews moving heavy equipment, warehouse and logistics staff on tight schedules, delivery drivers threading Glenoaks Boulevard, and office employees who spend part of the week commuting along I-5 or SR-134. When a shift ends with an injury, the next steps can feel murky. California generally sends an injured employee to workers' compensation, which pays regardless of fault and usually serves as the only remedy against the employer itself. That is not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver caused the harm, a separate third-party claim may sit alongside your comp benefits. Driving for work is a concrete example here. Burbank's 2025 public record lists 209 injury collisions and 297 people hurt, with volume clustering on I-5, SR-134, and Glenoaks Boulevard and a Friday peak between 5 and 7 p.m. We can sort out which claims fit your facts and review your options at no cost to you.

items.title: Comp and Third-Party Claims Sorted Out Together
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your only remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver may owe you more. We can look at both tracks.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Plainly
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and any third-party injury claim generally carries a two-year filing deadline. Knowing those dates early keeps your options open.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: It is illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery, and our consultation is always free.

items.question: I was rear-ended on the Golden State Freeway while making a work delivery in Burbank. Is that only a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of who was at fault. Since another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate personal injury claim against that driver, which carries California's two-year deadline. We can evaluate both so nothing gets left behind.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for a workplace injury in California?
items.answer: In most situations, no. Workers' compensation is designed to be the exclusive remedy against your employer, even when the employer was careless. The exceptions are narrow, so the more common route to additional recovery runs through a negligent third party such as a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment manufacturer.

items.question: What if my Burbank employer discourages me from reporting the injury?
items.answer: Report it anyway, in writing if you can, and try to do so within 30 days of the injury. California law prohibits an employer from firing, demoting, or otherwise retaliating against you for reporting a work injury or pursuing a claim. If that pressure continues, let us know, because retaliation can itself be a separate legal issue.
